rationale: C09 is a highly plausible material drafting template: it is an earlier Eisenhower disapproval of a broadly similar federal and postal employee pay bill and uses the same core argumentative sequence—acknowledging fair compensation, rejecting across-the-board increases because they perpetuate pay inequities, emphasizing substantial unfunded federal and postal costs, invoking broader personnel reforms and fringe benefits, and promising more discriminating recommendations to Congress. The overlap is far more concrete than shared subject matter and includes closely corresponding language and organization. C11 and C07 contain narrower parallels concerning uncoordinated pay scales and recruitment or retention, but neither approaches C09's comprehensive match.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Both would widen existing pay discrepancies within the Federal establishment and aggravate existing inequities
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the general pay increase proposed by this bill ignores and therefore tends to perpetuate the inequities we must correct
shared_material.explanation: Both reject a general salary increase because it would preserve or worsen structural inequities in federal pay scales.

shared_material.child_excerpt: During this same period, fringe benefits have grown substantially: low cost life insurance, unemployment compensation, liberalized retirement and survivor benefits.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: For the first time an inclusive system of Group Life Insurance and unemployment compensation benefits similar to those enjoyed by workers in private industry, have been provided for Federal employees.
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses C09's reliance on recently enacted fringe benefits as part of the case against the proposed pay increase.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The bills would increase annual expenditures by about $850 million for increased base pay and increased benefits computed on base pay.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: this measure would add $112 million to the cost of operating the Post Office Department... Likewise, this measure would add more than $200 million to Civil Service pay without providing any revenue to meet it.
shared_material.explanation: Both quantify the postal and classified-service fiscal burden and emphasize that the legislation supplies no adequate funding.

shared_material.child_excerpt: An inquiry into the need for adjustments in the structure of Executive Branch pay systems has been undertaken at my direction. In the event this inquiry demonstrates the need for logical, fair and discriminating adjustment, recommendations for appropriate action will be made early in the next session of the Congress.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I shall therefore resubmit to Congress when it convenes in January the recommendations previously made by the Administration, together with such additional recommendations as any change in conditions then existing may warrant.
shared_material.explanation: Both close by distinguishing rejection of the pending bill from opposition to all pay reform and promise better-targeted recommendations in the next congressional session.
